free.title: Baekjeong Black
free.caption:
JUST OPENED · KOREATOWN

Koreatown's most famous barbecue grill just came back bigger. Baekjeong Black opened September 23 with 8,000 square feet of tableside grilling and a cocktail bar tucked below it.

Same team, same neon-lit energy, now with a Wagyu and dry-aged beef menu the old spot never had. Order tableside and pick your grade - USDA Prime, dry-aged, or true Japanese Wagyu - while the staff does the actual grilling. Downstairs, Yangban pours Korean-inspired cocktails if you want a drink before your table's ready.

Tip: reservations aren't required, but the grill floor fills up fast after 7pm, so book ahead if you're going for dinner.

Send this to whoever's been missing K-Town's old grill.

📷 Whatnow NYC

food.title: Lunch Box Food Fair
food.caption:
FOOD · FIDI

Ten Lower Manhattan restaurants, ten dollars a box - the Financial District's Lunch Box food fair returns to Fosun Plaza on October 7.

Downtown Alliance lines up ten FiDi restaurants - Sadie's fried chicken, Sam Ping's Chinese BBQ, JoJu Vietnamese, Tacos del Barrio, and more - each serving one full boxed lunch for a flat $10, no matter what's inside. It runs 11:30am to 2:30pm at Fosun Plaza, 28 Liberty Street, and the popular boxes sell out before 1pm.

Tip: scope all ten stalls before you commit - you only get one line's worth of patience on a lunch break.

Send this to your office lunch group before the good boxes are gone.

📷 Downtown Alliance

art.title: LUMINISCENCE at St. Patrick's Cathedral
art.caption:
ART · MIDTOWN

St. Patrick's Cathedral is about to become a full-scale light show. LUMINISCENCE opens October 2, projecting 360-degree video mapping across the Gothic nave for a 60-minute performance with recorded, live choir, or full orchestra sessions.

Jonathan Roumie narrates three chapters tracing the cathedral's place in New York history, while the vaulted ceiling and stone spires - built in 1878 - light up in shifting color instead of stained glass. Tickets start at $44, with Live and Live+ sessions (choir and orchestra) at a premium.

Tip: Live+ tends to sell out first if you want the full orchestra experience.

Send this to whoever needs an excuse to get dressed up this fall.
